netstate.vd/news/oster.title: Oster bridge checkpoint to remain
netstate.vd/news/oster.body:
[b]Oster bridge checkpoint to remain in place[/b]

KESSEL - The Interior Ministry has confirmed that the security checkpoint on the [b]Oster River[/b] bridge will remain in place "for the foreseeable future".

"The Oster has always been a crossing for smugglers and provocateurs," a Ministry spokesman said. "Honest citizens pass through in minutes."

Citizens with information about suspicious activity near the river are asked to use the [url=go:netstate.vd/portal]Citizen Portal[/url].

netstate.vd/news/unity.title: Unity Bridge opened
netstate.vd/news/unity.body:
[b]Marshal opens the Unity Bridge[/b]

Thousands of grateful citizens lined the banks as Marshal Iosif Darvan cut the ribbon. "A nation that is connected is a nation that is safe," he said, to sustained applause lasting eleven minutes.

netstate.vd/news/vpn.title: Encryption: what citizens must know
netstate.vd/news/vpn.body:
[b]Encryption software: what every citizen must know[/b]

So-called "VPNs" and "encrypted messengers" hide criminal activity from the authorities who keep you safe.

From Thursday, possessing unregistered encryption software is a criminal offense.

[color=#7d8a99]Tip: a citizen who uses a VPN has something to hide. Know your neighbors.[/color]

netstate.vd/news/plant.title: Plant No. 2 medal
netstate.vd/news/plant.body:
[b]Truck Plant No. 2 receives Ministry medal[/b]

Shift boss A. Koval: "Our workers are the best in the Republic. Every truck we build is a truck for the nation."

A photograph shows the shift lined up in front of a new police van.

netstate.vd/marshal.title: Marshal Iosif Darvan
netstate.vd/marshal.body:
[font_size=20][b]Marshal Iosif Darvan[/b][/font_size]
[color=#7d8a99]Father of National Renewal[/color]

Born in a modest village, the young Iosif showed early genius in mathematics, poetry, agriculture and marksmanship. In 2030 he led the Night of Renewal that saved the Republic from chaos.

He has personally designed the national anthem, the national bird (the steel heron) and the Unity Bridge.

He sleeps three hours a night so that you may sleep eight.

[color=#7d8a99]This page is maintained by the Office of the Marshal. Interest in this page is appreciated.[/color]

netstate.vd/rules.title: Regulations
netstate.vd/rules.body:
[b]CURRENT REGULATIONS - KESSEL[/b]

- Internet cafes must record the ID of every customer.
- Curfew 23:00 - 05:00.
- Unregistered encryption software is a criminal offense.
- Oster bridge checkpoint: identity check, vehicle search, phone check.
- Gatherings of more than 5 people require a permit.
- Printing equipment must carry the citizen serial mark.

[color=#7d8a99]Regulations are updated for your safety.[/color]

[color=#c9a227]oldfox[/color] [color=#7d8a99](joined 6 years ago)[/color]

You post a picture of the checkpoint, they don't need to find YOU. They read the backpack, they find the PHONE. The phone has an owner.

Open the file's Properties before you post anything. If the backpack is full, empty it.

Scrub does it in one click: [url=dl:scrub]scrub.exe[/url]

lantern.vx/t/annex.title: the annex kiosk
lantern.vx/t/annex.body:
[b]the annex kiosk is still on factory settings[/b]

[color=#c9a227]kettle[/color] [color=#7d8a99](joined 4 years ago)[/color]
the interior ministry annex in kessel has a 'citizen records kiosk' in the lobby. you look up your own records on it. it's on the same office network as the archive.

nobody has updated it since 2033. the manual is on netstate, page 2. read page 2.

you'll want a proper tool: [url=dl:probe]probe.exe[/url]. map the network, poke things, get out.

three rules:
  1. every command makes noise. watch the trace meter.
  2. take what you need, not everything.
  3. `wipe logs` on the way out. always.

you didn't hear it from me.

if the station 4 list is in there, it's the current one. the copy going around is from march.
